name: Malkiah
title: Descendant of Priests After the Exile
summary: Malkiah (also spelled Malkijah) is a name that appears several times in the Old Testament, particularly in connection with the rebuilding of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. He is mentioned among those who worked to repair the walls of Jerusalem under Nehemiah's leadership and as a priest who participated in the covenant renewal ceremony. The name means 'my king is the Lord' and reflects a deep attachment to God.

keyEvents.title: Repair of the Dung Gate
keyEvents.description: Malkiah, son of Recab, ruler of the Beth-haccerem district, repaired the Dung Gate during the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned Among the Wall Builders
keyEvents.description: Malkiah is mentioned among those who took part in the great work of rebuilding Jerusalem's walls under Nehemiah's leadership, demonstrating his dedication to God's people.

keyEvents.title: Sealing of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: A man named Malkiah was among the priests and Levites who sealed the new covenant with God during Nehemiah's time.

keyEvents.title: Participation in the Dedication of the Wall
keyEvents.description: Malkia participated in the solemn dedication of the completed city wall in Jerusalem, an event marked by joy and praise.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Ezra's reform
keyEvents.description: A Malkia is mentioned among those who had taken foreign women as wives and were asked to send them away as part of Ezra's religious reform.

keyEvents.title: The imprisonment of the prophet Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: In the book of Jeremiah, Malkia, son of King Zedekiah, is mentioned in connection with the prophet Jeremiah being thrown into a well belonging to Malkia.
